symptom: `mxcli check -p` printed "Check passed!" (exit 0) for `create module role MyModule.Writer; create module role NoSuchModule.Reader;`; `exec` created MyModule.Writer, then failed with "module not found: NoSuchModule" (exit 1), leaving Writer in the model (reported on v0.25.0, Mendix 11.12.1). Issue mendixlabs/mxcli#1354
cause: validateWithContext's per-statement switch resolves the module of every module-scoped CREATE (entity, enumeration, microflow, …) but had no case for CreateModuleRoleStmt, and validateGrantReferences only resolves the roles a grant NAMES, never the statement that creates one — so nothing at check time looked up the module execCreateModuleRole stops on.
insight: **The check-tier gap is per statement type, so grep the switch for the AST type before reading any resolver.** `grep -n 'CreateModuleRoleStmt' mdl/executor/validate*.go` showed it only in the grant resolver's record/recordLater bookkeeping — the absence of a `case` in validateWithContext was the whole bug. Skip the plausible wrong turn of extending grantResolver: it resolves what a statement *names*, and widening it to the statement's own container would duplicate the findModule check every other CREATE already does in validate.go. Deliberately NOT extended to `drop module role`: execDropModuleRole calls findModule before honouring IF EXISTS, so exec refuses `drop module role if exists Missing.R` — which contradicts #531 (IF EXISTS tolerates a missing module); check mirroring that would lock in the exec inconsistency. Control: the pre-fix binary on PedApp printed "Created module role: Administration.Writer" then "Error: module not found: NoSuchModule"; fixed, the exec pre-flight refuses and Writer is absent. Repro `mdl-examples/bug-tests/1354-module-role-missing-module.mdl`.
